# Backtest reference fixtures

Frozen input (`input_series.csv`, seed 20260704, generated by `make_input.py`):
one GARCH(1,1)-t path (ω=.05, α=.09, β=.90, ν=8, n=1250 after 500 burn-in) with two
deterministic forecasters — `oracle` (true conditional VaR/ES) and `hs` (rolling
HS-250) — at α ∈ {1%, 2.5%, 5%}. Regenerating it invalidates every reference CSV.

| file | produced by | covers |
|---|---|---|
| `r_references.csv` | `make_r_references.R` (rugarch/GAS/esback, versions in `r_versions.txt`) | Kupiec UC, Christoffersen CC, rugarch ES boot, ESR 1–3, ER, CC |

Kupiec and Christoffersen are externally cross-checked against
rugarch/GAS-compatible references. The DQ implementation is validated by
formula-level and seeded size-property tests (`tests/test_dq_size.py`); no
external DQ fixture is claimed. (DQ(4) removed from the row above in the
v1.5 round: the CSV carries no dq rows — machine-verified 2026-07-22.)
| `quantlet_references.csv` | `make_quantlet_references.py` on QuantLet/HMD_ES @ `2490253e` | FZ0 mean loss (Pele & M-M-P convention) |

## Known discrepancy: QuantLet HMD_ES `kupiec_p` (documented 2026-07-04)

`code/pipeline.py::kupiec_p` in HMD_ES computes the null log-likelihood as
`n·ln(1−α) + x·ln(α)`; the Kupiec POF null term is `(n−x)·ln(1−α) + x·ln(α)`.
The LR is therefore inflated by `−2·x·ln(1−α)` (e.g. oracle @ α=5%, x=65, n=1250:
their LR 6.79 / p 0.0093 vs correct LR 0.10 / p 0.75 — confirmed by hand and against
rugarch/GAS on the same input). Consequently `quantlet_references.csv` keeps their
`kupiec_p` values ONLY to document the divergence; our `backtests.kupiec` is tested
against rugarch `VaRTest` and GAS `BacktestVaR`, which agree with the textbook formula.
Their `fz_loss` is the standard FZ0 (Patton–Ziegel–Chen, 0-homogeneous) and serves as
the binding FZ0 reference per proposal D1.
